opening: We're planning a tabletop for 20 port and logistics operations leaders, in four teams of five. It runs on 4 March 2027 from 09:00 to 13:00, with one 15-minute break. Most of them speak English as a second language, so keep everything plain.

answers.recording: Team answers are recorded; AI summarises them by theme for the after-action review
teachingPoints: Backup power is only as good as its last test
answers.problem: A heatwave cuts power to a regional data centre; port booking systems fail on and off, and leaders must decide who leads and what to tell shippers
answers.obviousExplanation: It looks like the heatwave overloaded the grid; really, the data centre's backup generators failed their last test and were never fixed
groundTruth: The backup generators failed their last test
Power is fully restored at 18:00 on Day 2
answers.attackPath: Not applicable: there is no attacker
answers.escalationCeiling: Never a full outage, nobody hurt, no cargo lost
answers.realVsFictional: Real: the season. Fictional: every port, company, person and number
answers.ending: Power restored and a generator repair planned before the deadline
answers.nationalBodies: By role only: your port authority, your ministry
answers.notionalNetwork: The port's corporate network and the crane control network, joined at the operations centre
answers.intent: Rehearse how the port's leaders decide and communicate when a data centre outage stops the cranes, and find the gaps in the continuity plan
answers.proficiency: Most have run the continuity plan once on paper; none have handled a real outage
answers.mandate: Keep the port operating safely and keep the public and partners informed; they can call in contractors and the regional authority
successCriteria: They agree a recovery priority within the first move
They hand over to the regional authority with a written brief
answers.victoryConditions: Success: cranes back and partners informed on time. Failure: the port goes silent for a whole move
answers.rulesOfEngagement: Decisions only; no real calls to outside organizations; stay within the continuity plan unless they say why
answers.deadline: The 18:00 ship departure; if the cranes are still down, the shipping line diverts
answers.description: A heatwave afternoon at a busy port goes wrong when the cranes stop. Leaders have to decide what to restore first and who to tell
answers.placeAndTime: A fictional mid-sized European port, a July afternoon in the present day
answers.population: Port staff, the shipping line, two reporters and the public on social media; about thirty voices
answers.informationEnvironment: Local news site, a regional radio station, social media posts from the public, staff email
keyEvents: Move 1: the cranes stop; White Cell; the team opens an incident
Move 2: a reporter calls; White Cell; the team agrees a holding line
decisionPoints: Move 1: restore cranes or the booking system first
Move 2: when to tell the public
answers.branching: If they tell the public early, the press calms; if late, a second reporter calls
escalationSteps: Shipping line threatens to divert (last recoverable)
answers.scenarioClock: Each move is two hours of scenario time
answers.fog: Partial: each role sees what it would
